The menu

Pick your finish —
here's what it actually means.

New to gel nails? Every card below explains the term in plain language, not just the name. Message on WhatsApp or Instagram for current pricing and availability.

Builder gel overlay

What it is: a soft gel painted straight onto your own natural nail — no fake tips added. It builds strength and a slight curve while still looking like your natural nail, just glossier and tougher.

French & milky finishes

What it is: French = a white line painted along the tip of a nude or pink nail. Milky = a sheer, milky-white colour washed over the whole nail for a soft, glassy look.

Hand-painted nail art

What it is: designs painted on freehand with a fine brush — dots, line work, gold detail — instead of stuck-on stickers. Fully custom to whatever idea you bring in.

3D florals & charms

What it is: small flowers sculpted up in gel or acrylic, plus rhinestones or charms pressed on top — texture you can actually feel, not just see.

Soft gel extensions

What it is: length added with a flexible gel tip attached to your natural nail, then shaped — almond, stiletto, square or coffin. Gentler on the nail than hard acrylic.

Acrylic vs. gel

What's the difference: acrylic is a powder-and-liquid mix that air-dries; gel is cured under a UV/LED lamp. Both add strength or length — Caitlynn will help you pick what suits your hands and your schedule.

Cat eye & chrome

What it is: cat eye is a magnetic polish dragged with a magnet before it cures, leaving a shimmering line of light that shifts as your hand moves. Chrome is a mirror-like powder buffed on top of gel.

Toes & touch-ups

What it is: pedicure-ready toe sets, plus quick infills or fixes to keep an existing set looking freshly done in between full appointments.

Still not sure what you want? That's completely normal — send a photo of anything you like the look of and Caitlynn will tell you what it's called and whether it'll work for you.
